newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty firms on currency selling, depos ease.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty firms on currency selling, depos ease.

text.p: The zloty gradually gained against the basket of currencies on Tuesday amid a dollar selling trend likely sparked by a large privatisation deal, dealers said.
On November 7, today's spot transaction value date, South Korea's LG Group, is to take over its majority stake in Poland's Petrobank SA paying nearly $50 million.
Dealers said the zloty's gains were not fuelled by foreign investor purchases of Polish T-bills and did not correspond with dollar/mark trends in European trade.
"The zloty inched up against world markets trends," said Jaroslaw Dryjski from Bank Slaski SA.
The zloty closed at 2.07/2.02 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than Monday's 1.95/1.92 percent from parity.
It was at 2.8085/05 to the dollar, up from 2.8125/30 on Monday and at 1.8525/50 to the mark, up from 1.8575/85.
"The zloty may have firmed on a privatisation deal," said a dealer at a large Polish bank.

Dealers said the Polish forex market will focus on news from the U.S. presidential elections after immediate concern over Russian President Boris Yeltsin's health subsided following initial reports that his heart surgery succeeded.
On the money market one-day deposit rates fell slightly after banks squared reserve positions, but dealers said there was some demand for longer two-week and three month depos.
Overnight rates were at 19.95/20.10 percent lower than opening's 20.00/20.20 percent. Tomorrow/next rates were at 19.85/20.10 percent, down from 20.0/20.3 percent.
Dealers said longer deposit rates may rise in the near-term in line with the expected tightening of the central bank's monetary policy within the next several months.
"It seems banks expect market rates may rise in the longer term," said Alicja Wolanska from Raiffeisen Centrobank.
